examples.text: Deine Schwester hat mir eine spannende Geschichte erzählt
examples.translation: Twoja siostra opowiedziała mi ekscytującą historię.

examples.text: Eine spannende Geschichte

examples.translation: Les films de Spielberg sont toujours captivants.

examples.text: (...) seit Jahren gibt es Kritik, dass die Formel 1 immer mehr an Charakter verliert. Nun steuert die FIA dagegen und kündigt eine spannende Neuerung für die aktuelle Saison an: Künftig soll es bei allen Rennen Gegenverkehr geben.
examples.translation: (...) depuis des années, des critiques s’élèvent pour dire que la Formule 1 perd de plus en plus de son caractère. La FIA s'y oppose désormais et annonce une nouveauté intéressante pour la saison en cours : A l’avenir, dans toutes les courses il y aura de la circulation en sens inverse.

glosses: Spannung (Erregung, Neugier) hervorrufend, oft ein (meist) angenehmes Gefühl des Grusels oder der gebannten Faszination erzeugend

examples.text: Spannende Abenteuer erwarten Sie in unserem Erlebnispark.
Der Chef erhofft sich spannende neue Vorschläge von den neuen jungen Mitarbeitern.

glosses: present participle and gerund of thrill
Causing a feeling of sudden excitement.

examples.text: He was thinking; but the glory of the song, the swell from the great organ, the clustered lights, […], the height and vastness of this noble fane, its antiquity and its strength—all these things seemed to have their part as causes of the thrilling emotion that accompanied his thoughts.
[…] my heart told me that she did all be stirred with small thrillings of defiance unto me, and with thrillings of love […]

glosses: present participle and gerund of excite

examples.text: Some of the most exciting games ever played have ended in draws.
Among the Turks, an exciting compound consists of olibanum, myrrh, camphor, musk, in pulverized form. The resultant perfume is said to affect the genitals.

glosses: The process of something becoming excited; excitation.

examples.text: But parents and masters should make haste in this, as to a great purchase for their children and servants; which while they defer, both sides suffer; the one, in wanting many excitings of grace, the other, in being worse served and obeyed.
a gripping action film

glosses: present participle and gerund of grip
The act of forming a grip.

examples.text: His resentful comments on this conviction were greeted only by great tears falling in silence, and almost convulsive grippings of his hand.

glosses: Obsolete form of griping (“pinching and spasmodic pain in the intestines”).

examples.text: The same Night it began to operate by Grippings and Sweating, and he being bred a Surgeon, took some Medicines to correct the Grippings, which in some Measure the Medicine did, but he lost his Appetite […]

glosses: present participle and gerund of enthrall

examples.text: The Abbess had not miscalculated the effect of the yesterday's ceremony—she knew it was not binding, but its influence as a religious obligation was enthralling to a degree.

Glittering castles in Spain were shaping themselves out of the mists and rainbows of her lively fancy; adventures wonderful and enthralling were happening to her in cloudland—adventures that always turned out triumphantly and never involved her in scrapes like those of actual life.
Andre Santos equalised and the outstanding Theo Walcott put Arsenal ahead for the first time before Juan Mata's spectacular strike set up the finale for an enthralling encounter.

glosses: Engrossing; fascinating; gaining rapt attention; captivating.

examples.text: Cuphead built a reputation for difficulty before release, but its boss battles are mostly about recognizing patterns than getting lucky against unfair bosses. Watching players ace their way through the game’s bosses is a spellbinding reminder that even tough games can be defeated easily with hard work.

There is no doubt that recent developments in generative AI and large language models that produce text, information and images—and Shakespearean sonnets—in response to simple user prompts are impressive and even spellbinding.

glosses: Having the power to bind magically through the agency of a spell.

examples.text: Salt is a very favoured ingredient of spell-binding concoctions.

glosses: A spell or enchantment that restrains or constricts someone's actions or freedom of will.

examples.text: The Roman epic poet Vergil refers to the incapacitating effects of ligatures, while Ovid, the erotic poet, admits the power of such spell-bindings.

examples.text: Jestem ciekawy, gdzie znajdziecie otwarty sklep o tej porze.

examples.text: Увлекательный темперамент, красивый голос (сопрано) и художественность исполнения сделали артистку одной из лучших сил Спб. оперы (партии свои она поёт на русском языке).

glosses: Que causa emoción, estimula o conmueve de manera particular y generalmente intensa.

examples.text: He indeed had good reason to be offended; for though Dr. Swinfen's motive was good, he inconsiderately betrayed a matter deeply interesting and of great delicacy, which had been entrusted to him in conference […].

glosses: Arousing or holding the attention or interest of someone.

examples.text: Cricket is not interesting to watch.

glosses: present participle and gerund of interest
